name: Asakusa
tagline: Tokyo in 15 minutes and Otemachi in 17 minutes. Served by 3 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Taito City, where Tobu, Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 3 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 17 minutes to Otemachi, 28 minutes to Shinjuku, 35 minutes to Shibuya and 27 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 3.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.4 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 3.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.4 m to 4.8 m, a difference of 3.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 5 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: マイカイマート　ロヂャース

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 9 clinics and 28 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 浅草寺病院, about 10 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 墨田病院, about 12 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 3 lines serve the station. Tobu Skytree Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line also call here. Toei Asakusa Line are available too. The lines are split between operators (Tobu runs 1 line, Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is not on. Tobu Skytree Line runs at 142%. Its busiest stretch is 小菅→北千住, which this station is likewise not on. Toei Asakusa Line runs at 123% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 本所吾妻橋→浅草, which includes this station. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000 and 2LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. 3 lines and a wide choice of connections and plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, a large projected flood depth and many bars by the station and voices outside late at night holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For how easy the shopping is, Asakusa (Tsukuba Express); for rail connections, Asakusa.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Asakusa. Asakusa (Tsukuba Express) has only the Tsukuba Express, so Asakusa is the better connected. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. On how easy the shopping is, though, Asakusa (Tsukuba Express) comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For quiet, Tawaramachi; for rail connections, Asakusa.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Asakusa. Tawaramachi has only the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, so Asakusa is the better connected. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat also costs about ¥10,000 more at Tawaramachi. On quiet, though, Tawaramachi comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: The 首都高速6号向島線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
江戸通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 3 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
